Title: Initialize the TypeScript monorepo
User Story: As a SmartTest contributor, I want a pnpm workspace with strict TypeScript, project references and Vitest, so that every package builds and tests the same way.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Given a fresh clone, when I run `pnpm i && pnpm build`, then all packages compile with `strict` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` enabled
- `pnpm test` runs Vitest across packages resolving workspace sources without a prior build
- Node engines are pinned to the supported LTS range and enforced

Title: Define and enforce package boundaries
User Story: As a tech lead, I want the package map and allowed dependency directions to be machine-checked, so that the core never depends on CLI, UI or AI packages.
Acceptance Criteria:
- The manifest `scripts/packages.manifest.json` is the single source of truth and the scaffolder rejects cycles
- CI fails when a package imports a workspace package not declared in its manifest deps
- `core` has no dependency on any `ai-*` or `studio-*` package (ADR-0004)

Title: Configuration contract, loader and schema validation
User Story: As a developer, I want a typed `smarttest.config.ts` with clear validation errors, so that misconfiguration is caught before anything runs.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `defineConfig()` gives editor completion for every 1.0 option
- Config is discovered from `smarttest.config.{ts,mts,js,mjs,json}` or `--config`
- Invalid config produces an `ST_CONFIG_INVALID` error listing every offending path with a hint, exit code 3
- Unknown keys produce warnings, not silent acceptance

Title: Linting, formatting and strict typing gates
User Story: As a SmartTest contributor, I want one fast lint/format tool wired into CI and pre-commit, so that reviews focus on behavior, not style.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `pnpm lint` (Biome) passes on a clean tree and fails CI on violations
- `pnpm format` is idempotent
- Editor settings are committed for VS Code

Title: Fixture project catalogue
User Story: As a QA engineer, I want realistic, versioned fixture repositories covering the 1.0 compatibility matrix, so that every engine is tested against the projects we claim to support.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Fixtures exist for: TS library (Vitest), React (Vitest), Next.js (Jest), Express CJS (Jest), NestJS (Jest), pnpm monorepo, Yarn ESM, no-VCS project
- Each fixture has an `expected.json` describing detection results and known test↔source relationships
- A helper materialises a fixture into a temp dir with an optional Git history script

Title: Continuous integration pipeline
User Story: As a SmartTest contributor, I want CI on every PR across Linux, macOS and Windows and supported Node LTS versions, so that cross-platform regressions are caught before merge.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Workflow runs lint, typecheck, test and `planning:build --check`
- Matrix covers ubuntu, macos, windows × Node 22 and 24
- Workflows use pinned actions and least-privilege `permissions`

Title: Structured logging with secret redaction
User Story: As a developer, I want useful `--verbose` logs that never leak secrets, so that I can debug SmartTest safely and share logs.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Logger supports levels, scoped child loggers and JSON output
- Values matching token/key patterns and configured env names are redacted in every sink
- Logs are written to `.smarttest/logs/` with rotation

Title: Stable error model and exit codes
User Story: As a CI maintainer, I want documented, versioned exit codes and error identifiers, so that pipelines can react to failure categories reliably.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `SmartTestError` carries a stable `code`, `category` and optional `hint`
- Exit codes 0/1/2/3/4/5/70 are documented in the CLI reference and locked by a test
- Unexpected errors map to 70 and print a bug-report hint

Title: Plugin SDK foundation and capability model
User Story: As a plugin author, I want typed contracts for language, test-runner and VCS adapters with explicit capabilities, so that new ecosystems can be added without changing the core.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `TestAdapter`, `LanguageAdapter` and `VersionControlAdapter` contracts are exported from `@smarttest/plugin-sdk`
- Every capability is `true | false | "partial"`; undeclared means unsupported
- A conformance test-kit helper exists that adapters can run against fixtures

Title: Architecture documentation and ADRs
User Story: As a new contributor, I want an architecture overview and recorded decisions, so that I understand why the system looks the way it does.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `documentation/architecture/overview.md` describes layers, packages and data flow
- ADR-0001…0007 are written and reviewed
- Each package README links its epic and architecture context

Title: Verify product name and npm package availability
User Story: As a product owner, I want confirmation that we can publish as `smarttest` (or a fallback), so that we don't build a brand we can't ship.
Acceptance Criteria:
- npm availability of `smarttest`, `@smarttest/*` scope and fallbacks is checked and recorded (`smarttest` was unpublished and may be claimable)
- A basic trademark/collision search is recorded
- Decision recorded in ADR-0007 with the chosen name and scope

Title: Spike: TypeScript analysis engine
User Story: As a tech lead, I want a time-boxed comparison of the TS 6 Compiler API, the TS 7 native API and tree-sitter, so that the source-intelligence epic starts on a sound, future-proof base.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Spike measures cold/warm parse time and memory on the monorepo fixture for each option
- Reports what each option can resolve (aliases, project references, type-only imports)
- Outcome recorded in ADR-0002 with a migration note for TS 7

Title: Spike: local intelligence store
User Story: As a tech lead, I want to choose between `node:sqlite` and `better-sqlite3` for the local store, so that installation stays frictionless on every OS.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Benchmark insert/query of 100k edges for each option
- Install works without a compiler toolchain on the CI matrix
- Outcome recorded in ADR-0003

Title: Command framework, global flags and help
User Story: As a developer, I want a consistent `smarttest <command>` interface with discoverable help, so that I can learn the tool from the terminal.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Global flags `--config --workspace --json --quiet --verbose --non-interactive --dry-run --help` are parsed uniformly
- Unknown commands/flags exit 2 with a 'did you mean' suggestion
- `smarttest --version` and `smarttest help <command>` work
- Warm startup for `--help` is under 300 ms on the reference machine

Title: Output modes for humans and machines
User Story: As a CI maintainer, I want colored, compact output in a TTY and plain/JSON output elsewhere, so that the same command works locally and in pipelines.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Non-TTY output contains no ANSI codes or spinners and never prompts
- `--json` prints exactly one JSON document on stdout; logs go to stderr
- `NO_COLOR` and `FORCE_COLOR` are respected

Title: Interactive root menu
User Story: As a developer new to SmartTest, I want `smarttest` with no arguments to show a searchable menu of common actions, so that I don't have to memorise commands.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Menu shows workspace name, status and the actions: run affected, generate architecture, coverage & reports, diagnostics, settings
- Arrow keys, Enter and `/` search work; Esc exits
- In non-TTY or `--non-interactive`, `smarttest` prints help and exits 0

Title: Progress and diagnostics renderer
User Story: As a developer, I want clear progress for long steps and structured, actionable errors, so that I always know what SmartTest is doing and how to fix problems.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Long-running phases render a task list with durations
- Errors print code, message, hint and docs link; `--verbose` adds the cause chain
- Warnings are summarised at the end of a command

Title: `smarttest scan` command
User Story: As a developer, I want a read-only command that shows what SmartTest understands about my project, so that I can verify detection and indexing before trusting selection.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Prints project profile, VCS state, file/symbol/edge counts and unresolved imports
- `--json` output is schema-versioned
- Never writes outside `.smarttest/`

Title: Runtime environment scan
User Story: As a developer, I want SmartTest to detect OS, CPU, memory, Node version and permissions, so that it can choose sane worker counts and warn about unsupported runtimes.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Returns OS, arch, Node version, CPU count, free memory and writable state of the project root
- Unsupported Node versions produce an actionable diagnostic
- Environment variables are only read from an allow-list; values never logged

Title: Package manager and workspace detection
User Story: As a developer in a monorepo, I want npm, pnpm and Yarn projects and their workspaces to be detected, so that SmartTest understands package boundaries.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Detects npm/pnpm/Yarn (classic & berry) from lockfiles and `packageManager`
- Lists workspace packages with names, paths and internal dependencies
- Conflicting lockfiles produce a warning, not a guess

Title: Framework detection with evidence
User Story: As a developer, I want React, Next.js, Express, NestJS and plain Node libraries recognised, so that recommendations fit my stack.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Each detected framework lists its evidence (manifest dep, config file, import)
- Unknown frameworks don't block detection; the project is treated as generic Node
- Detection results match `expected.json` for every fixture

Title: Test runner and test convention detection
User Story: As a QA engineer, I want Jest/Vitest, their configs, test file patterns, setup files and placement conventions detected, so that SmartTest reuses what already exists.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Detects Jest and Vitest including config files and per-workspace configs
- Infers placement convention (mirror / colocated / mixed) with ratios
- Lists fixtures, mocks and setup files without modifying them

Title: Source layout and import alias analysis
User Story: As a developer, I want source roots, entry points, generated dirs and path aliases detected, so that analysis covers the right files.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Reads `tsconfig` paths/baseUrl, package `exports`/`imports` and bundler aliases where statically declared
- Proposes include/exclude globs; generated/build dirs excluded by default
- Ambiguities are reported as warnings with evidence

Title: Version control detection
User Story: As a developer, I want Git, nested repositories and no-VCS projects detected, so that the right change source is chosen automatically.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Detects Git root, worktrees and nested repos; reports repository boundaries
- SVN/Mercurial/Perforce markers are detected and reported as 'not supported in 1.0'
- No VCS → native snapshots recommended

Title: Coverage provider and CI detection
User Story: As a CI maintainer, I want existing coverage providers and CI config files detected, so that SmartTest integrates without duplicating setup.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Detects v8/istanbul providers and reporter config for Jest and Vitest
- Detects GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins and Azure Pipelines files
- Results feed the setup recommendation engine

Title: VCS adapter contract and normalized ChangeSet
User Story: As a plugin author, I want a provider-neutral change model with explicit completeness, so that the impact engine never depends on Git specifics.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `ChangeSet` supports added/modified/deleted/renamed with optional ranges and hashes
- `completeness` is mandatory; partial results carry warnings
- Revision refs are provider-scoped and cannot be compared across providers

Title: Git branch and commit comparison
User Story: As a developer, I want `--base main` and commit-range comparisons, so that I can test exactly what my branch changes.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `--base <ref>` compares against the merge-base by default; `--base-mode=direct` compares directly
- Changed line ranges are produced for modified files
- Shallow clones without the base produce a clear error with a fetch hint (exit 4)

Title: Git staged, uncommitted and untracked changes
User Story: As a developer, I want `--staged` and `--uncommitted` modes, so that I get fast feedback before committing.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `--staged` uses the index only; `--uncommitted` includes working tree + untracked (respecting .gitignore)
- Binary files are reported but not parsed
- Results are identical to `git diff` on the fixture scenarios

Title: Git renames, deletions, worktrees and nested repos
User Story: As a developer, I want renames and deletions handled correctly in all repo shapes, so that moved code doesn't look like brand-new code.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Renames carry `previousPath`; deletions mark dependent tests as affected
- Works from a linked worktree and inside a monorepo sub-package
- Nested repositories are not silently mixed; each boundary is reported

Title: Native snapshot baseline and content fingerprints
User Story: As a developer without version control, I want SmartTest to track changes using its own snapshots, so that intelligent selection works in any folder.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `snapshot create` stores content hashes (not copies by default) under `.smarttest/state/`
- Incremental fingerprinting uses mtime+size pre-checks and content hashes to confirm
- Rename detection by content hash for unchanged files
- Snapshots are deduplicated and never copy the whole repository

Title: Snapshot comparison with completeness reporting
User Story: As a developer, I want to diff the working tree against a snapshot, so that I see exactly what changed since my last verified run.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `snapshot diff [id]` produces a normalized ChangeSet
- When content is not stored, changed ranges are reported as unknown and completeness = partial
- A snapshot is labelled 'verified baseline' only when linked to execution evidence

Title: Hybrid mode: Git + native snapshots
User Story: As a developer, I want Git revisions plus native snapshots for local incremental analysis, so that repeated local runs are fast between commits.
Acceptance Criteria:
- In hybrid mode, local runs diff against the last snapshot; `--base` diffs against Git
- Snapshot ids are never treated as Git commits
- Mode is visible in `vcs status`

Title: `snapshot` and `vcs` commands
User Story: As a developer, I want commands to create, list, inspect, diff snapshots and inspect VCS state, so that change tracking is transparent.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `snapshot create|list|inspect|diff` and `vcs detect|status` implemented with `--json`
- `vcs connect` switches the provider explicitly
- Every command documented in the CLI reference

Title: Snapshot retention and prune
User Story: As a developer, I want old snapshots pruned by a retention policy, so that `.smarttest/` doesn't grow without bounds.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `snapshot prune` honours `keep`/`maxAge` config and never deletes verified baselines without `--force`
- Dry-run lists what would be removed
- Prune is safe to interrupt

Title: TypeScript program loader
User Story: As a developer, I want SmartTest to load my TS project exactly as `tsc` sees it, so that aliases, project references and type-only imports are understood.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Honours tsconfig `extends`, `paths`, `references` and per-package configs
- Type-only imports are recorded with a `type-only` flag
- Files outside include globs are not analysed

Title: JavaScript parsing for ESM, CJS and JSX
User Story: As a developer with a JS codebase, I want plain JS projects analysed too, so that I don't need TypeScript to benefit.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Parses ESM `import`/`export`, CJS `require`/`module.exports` and JSX
- Dynamic `import()` and computed `require()` are recorded as unresolved with reason
- Express CJS fixture produces the expected relationships

Title: Symbol index
User Story: As a SmartTest engine, I want every module, class, function, method, property and type indexed with stable ids, so that impact can be computed below file level.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Symbols follow the `SourceSymbol` model with stable ids across unrelated edits
- Qualified names are unique within a workspace
- Index for each fixture matches its golden snapshot

Title: Import resolution
User Story: As a developer, I want imports resolved through aliases, workspaces, `exports` maps and barrel files, so that dependencies across packages are not missed.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Resolves relative, alias, workspace-package and `exports`-conditioned imports
- Barrel re-exports are followed to the defining symbol
- Every unresolved import is recorded with file, specifier and reason — never dropped

Title: Class, method and decorator analysis
User Story: As a NestJS developer, I want classes, methods, inheritance and decorators analysed, so that rules and selection can target `*Service` methods precisely.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Captures extends/implements, constructor-injected dependencies and decorators with arguments
- Method visibility is recorded
- NestJS fixture produces the expected class graph

Title: Export and public API analysis
User Story: As a library author, I want the public API surface of each package computed, so that exported-API changes trigger broader verification.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Public API = symbols reachable from package entry points/`exports`
- Exported vs internal is a symbol attribute
- API surface diff is available to semantic diff

Title: Semantic diff with uncertainty
User Story: As a developer, I want changes classified (comment-only, formatting, implementation, signature, exported API…), so that trivial edits don't trigger large test runs and risky ones do.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Classifies every §9.4 kind and maps changed ranges to symbols
- Each classification has a confidence; anything unclear is `unclassifiable` (never 'no-op')
- Comment/formatting-only changes are only treated as no-op in FAST mode, never in SAFE

Title: Incremental parsing and persistent index
User Story: As a developer, I want only changed and invalidated files re-parsed, so that warm analysis stays fast on large repos.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Second run with one changed file re-parses only that file and its invalidated dependents
- Index invalidates on tsconfig/package.json changes
- Warm diff analysis < 500 ms on the medium benchmark repo

Title: Generated-code policies
User Story: As a developer, I want generated directories handled by explicit rules, so that build output never pollutes the graph.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Config option `generated: [{ path, policy: exclude | test-source | rebuild-required }]`
- Detected generated dirs (e.g. `.next`, `dist`) are excluded by default
- Changes to a generator's input mark `rebuild-required` outputs as affected

Title: Graph model with provenance and confidence
User Story: As a SmartTest engine, I want typed nodes and edges carrying provenance and confidence, so that evidence is never mixed without trace.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Supports all §10.2 node kinds and §10.3 edge kinds
- Every edge has `provenance` and `confidence`; unknown stays unknown
- Uncertainty metadata (unresolved imports, dynamic patterns) attaches to nodes

Title: Persistent graph storage
User Story: As a developer, I want the graph persisted locally, so that warm runs don't rebuild everything.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Graph stored in `.smarttest/state/index.db` with a schema version and migrations
- Corrupt or incompatible stores are detected and rebuilt with a warning
- Writes are transactional

Title: Reverse and transitive traversal with cycle safety
User Story: As a SmartTest engine, I want fast reverse-dependency and transitive queries, so that every test reachable from a change is found.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Reverse traversal returns paths, not only node sets
- Cycles terminate and are reported
- Warm selection query < 200 ms on the medium benchmark repo

Title: Incremental graph updates
User Story: As a developer, I want the graph updated incrementally after changes, so that analysis cost scales with the change, not the repo.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Updating one file rewrites only its nodes/edges in one transaction
- Result is identical to a full rebuild (property test over fixture edits)
- Batch updates are supported for large change sets

Title: Graph snapshots, query API and `smarttest graph`
User Story: As a developer, I want to query and export the graph, so that I can inspect relationships and feed future visual tools.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `smarttest graph --from <symbol|file> --direction dependents|dependencies --depth n`
- Export to JSON and DOT
- Graph snapshots can be associated with native snapshots

Title: Vitest adapter
User Story: As a Vitest user, I want SmartTest to discover and run my Vitest tests through Vitest itself, so that I keep my runner, config and plugins.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Discovers test files and test cases using the project's Vitest config
- Runs a file selection (and test-case selection where supported) and returns normalized results
- Declares capabilities honestly; results match a native `vitest run` on fixtures

Title: Jest adapter
User Story: As a Jest user, I want SmartTest to discover and run my Jest tests through Jest itself, so that I keep my runner, config and transforms.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Discovers tests using the project's Jest config, including multi-project configs
- Runs file selections and returns normalized results
- Results match a native `jest` run on fixtures

Title: Normalized test model and honest result statuses
User Story: As a developer, I want one test model and status vocabulary across runners, so that reports never misrepresent what happened.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Statuses: passed, failed, skipped, pending, cancelled, timed-out, flaky, infrastructure-error (cached-* reserved)
- 'Skipped by selection' is distinct from 'skipped by the test' and is never counted as passed
- Runner crashes map to infrastructure-error, exit code 4

Title: Test-to-source mapping (TESTS edges)
User Story: As a SmartTest engine, I want test files linked to the source symbols they import and exercise statically, so that selection can walk from code to tests.
Acceptance Criteria:
- TESTS edges created from test-file imports to symbols, including through mocks (`vi.mock`/`jest.mock` recorded as uncertainty)
- Test files with no resolvable target are flagged
- Mapping matches `expected.json` relationships on fixtures

Title: Scheduling, timeouts and cancellation
User Story: As a developer, I want selected tests run in parallel with timeouts and clean cancellation, so that runs are fast and Ctrl-C never leaves orphans.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Worker count derives from CPU/memory unless configured
- Global and per-run timeouts produce `timed-out` statuses
- SIGINT cancels child processes and reports `cancelled` within 2 s

Title: Retry policies and flaky marking
User Story: As a QA engineer, I want configurable retries where a pass-after-fail stays visibly flaky, so that instability is surfaced, not hidden.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `retries` configurable globally and by rule
- A test that fails then passes is reported as `flaky`, never as plain `passed`
- Flaky occurrences are recorded in `.smarttest/runs/`

Title: Execution and analysis telemetry (local only)
User Story: As a developer, I want timings for every phase recorded locally, so that I can see SmartTest's overhead versus its savings.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Records scan, parse, graph update, impact, discovery, execution and report durations and peak memory
- Nothing leaves the machine; no telemetry is sent anywhere
- Timings appear in JSON/HTML reports

Title: Direct test selection
User Story: As a developer, I want tests that directly target changed symbols selected, so that the most relevant tests always run.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Changed test files are always selected
- Tests with a TESTS edge to a changed symbol are selected with reason `direct-dependency`
- Output conforms to `ImpactDecision`

Title: Transitive test selection
User Story: As a developer, I want tests reachable through dependents selected, so that regressions in callers are caught.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Selection includes tests reachable via reverse IMPORTS/CALLS/EXTENDS/INSTANTIATES edges
- Each selected test carries the graph path as evidence
- Depth limits are mode-dependent and reported

Title: Mandatory selection triggers
User Story: As a tech lead, I want broad verification forced for global-impact changes, so that config and dependency changes can't slip through.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Changes to tsconfig, runner config, package manifests/lockfiles, env config and global setup files trigger the full suite (or configured scope)
- Each trigger is reported with reason `mandatory-trigger`
- Rules can add triggers but cannot remove built-in ones

Title: Safe fallback on partial analysis
User Story: As a developer, I want SmartTest to widen or run everything when it isn't sure, so that uncertainty never silently drops tests.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Unresolved imports/dynamic patterns touching the change trigger fallback per mode
- `analysisStatus` = partial/fallback and `fallbackApplied` = true are reported
- Fallback reason is printed in the summary

Title: FAST, BALANCED and SAFE modes
User Story: As a developer, I want to choose a safety mode per run, rule or CI context, so that local feedback is fast and releases are strict.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `--mode fast|balanced|safe`; default balanced
- SAFE widens selection, ignores comment-only optimisations and forces full suite on any uncertainty
- Mode used is shown in output and reports

Title: Risk classification
User Story: As a tech lead, I want changes classified by risk using rules and change kind, so that critical code is treated more conservatively.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Risk = max(rule risk, change-kind risk)
- Critical risk upgrades the effective mode to SAFE for affected areas
- Risk appears in explain output

Title: Selection explanations: `smarttest explain`
User Story: As a developer, I want to ask why any test was selected or skipped, so that I can trust — or challenge — every decision.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `smarttest explain <test>` lists reasons (symbols, paths, rules, triggers) for selected tests
- For skipped tests it lists why plus a confidence statement bounded by the dependency model
- `--json` exposes the full reason objects

Title: `smarttest run --affected` and `smarttest impact`
User Story: As a developer, I want one command to analyse changes and run only affected tests, so that I get the core value of SmartTest.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `run --affected` = change detection → impact → execution → summary
- `impact` prints the decision without running tests
- `run --all` runs the full suite through the same pipeline
- Summary shows selected, executed, skipped (not run), passed, failed and duration

Title: `smarttest validate-selection`
User Story: As a team lead evaluating SmartTest, I want to compare a selective run against a full reference run, so that I have evidence before trusting selection in CI.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Runs selection and full suite on the same change and compares outcomes
- Reports selected, skipped, failures found, failures missed, time saved, analysis overhead, flaky interference
- Any missed failure exits 5 and prints the dependency gap

Title: Rule schema, scopes and core selectors
User Story: As a tech lead, I want rules by path, package, module, class, function and method, so that testing policies follow our architecture.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Rules match by path glob, package, class/function/method name patterns
- Rules may declare `require`, `coverage`, `risk`, `execution`, `generate`
- Rule evaluation for a symbol is a pure function with golden tests

Title: Deterministic precedence and conflict detection
User Story: As a tech lead, I want predictable outcomes when rules overlap, so that policies can't silently weaken each other.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Precedence: specificity, then declaration order; documented
- Mandatory safeguards cannot be weakened by lower-priority rules
- Conflicting templates/destinations raise `ST_RULE_CONFLICT` (exit 3)

Title: Decorator, visibility, kind and inheritance selectors
User Story: As a NestJS developer, I want rules like 'every `@Controller` needs integration tests', so that framework conventions map to policies.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Selectors for decorator, visibility, symbol kind, implements/extends
- Selectors combine with AND semantics
- Covered by golden tests on the NestJS fixture

Title: Coverage, criticality and execution policies
User Story: As a tech lead, I want rules to require test categories, coverage thresholds and always-run behavior, so that critical areas get stronger protection.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `execution.alwaysRunOnAffected` and `execution.mode` honoured by the impact engine
- Missing required test categories are reported as policy findings
- Coverage thresholds are evaluated when coverage is available, otherwise reported as 'not evaluated'

Title: `rules list | validate | explain`
User Story: As a developer, I want to inspect which rules apply to a file or symbol and why, so that policy decisions are transparent.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `rules list` shows all rules with scope and source
- `rules validate` checks schema and conflicts
- `rules explain <path|symbol>` shows matched rules, precedence and effective policy

Title: Setup recommendation engine
User Story: As a developer, I want a recommended setup plan with a reason for every choice, so that I understand and trust what init proposes.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Plan covers layout, naming, adapters, coverage provider, include/exclude, impact mode, snapshots, store dir, workers and suggested rules
- Every recommendation has a reason and evidence
- Warnings list untested modules and global-impact config files

Title: `smarttest init` wizard and setup modes
User Story: As a developer, I want interactive, automatic, advanced and non-interactive init, so that setup fits my context, including CI.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Interactive mode shows the plan and lets me accept/edit each section
- `--auto` applies only low-risk actions; `--advanced` exposes all options
- `--yes --non-interactive` never prompts; missing required input exits 3 deterministically

Title: Init dry-run and change preview
User Story: As a cautious developer, I want to see every file init would create or modify, so that nothing surprises me.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `init --dry-run` prints a diff of every change and writes nothing (verified by FS snapshot)
- Preview distinguishes create / modify / skip-existing
- Same plan is produced by dry-run and real run

Title: Safe configuration writing
User Story: As a developer, I want init to merge into my existing files safely, so that my configuration and scripts are preserved.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Atomic writes (temp + rename); package.json scripts merged without duplicates or reformatting unrelated keys
- Name collisions detected; existing files never replaced without explicit approval
- `.smarttest/` added to .gitignore; no dependency major upgrades; no install hooks executed

Title: Setup validation and setup report
User Story: As a developer, I want init to verify the setup works and summarise what it did, so that I know I'm ready to run.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Validates config schema and that the chosen adapter discovers tests
- Writes `.smarttest/reports/setup.md` with actions, warnings and next steps
- Unsupported setups produce actionable diagnostics instead of partial installs

Title: Idempotent init
User Story: As a developer, I want re-running init to be harmless, so that I can safely re-run it after upgrades.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Second run on an initialised fixture produces zero changes
- User edits to generated config are preserved
- Covered by a test across all 8 fixtures

Title: Init rollback
User Story: As a developer, I want to undo what init changed, so that trying SmartTest is risk-free.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Init records a change journal in `.smarttest/state/init-journal.json`
- `init --rollback` restores modified files and removes created ones (if unmodified since)
- Files edited after init are reported, not overwritten

Title: `smarttest doctor`
User Story: As a developer, I want a diagnostic command that checks my setup, so that I can fix problems without reading source code.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Checks runtime, config validity, adapter discovery, VCS state, store health and stale index
- Each finding has severity, explanation and fix hint
- Exit code reflects worst finding category

Title: Mirror and colocated layouts
User Story: As a developer, I want test paths computed from source paths using mirror or colocated layout, so that my test tree stays organised automatically.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Mirror maps `src/modules/auth/AuthService.ts` → `tests/unit/modules/auth/AuthService.test.ts`
- Colocated maps to `src/modules/auth/AuthService.test.ts`
- The detected existing convention is the default

Title: Domain and custom layouts with naming tokens
User Story: As a tech lead, I want domain grouping and custom path templates, so that the generator fits our conventions.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Tokens `{ClassName} {FunctionName} {MethodName} {FileName} {ModuleName} {PackageName} {DomainName} {Type} {Extension}` supported
- Invalid templates fail validation with the offending token
- Domain layout groups by configured domain mapping

Title: Class and module templates
User Story: As a developer, I want templates per symbol type (service, controller, repository, util), so that scaffolds start with the right structure.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Built-in templates for Jest and Vitest; selection driven by rules `generate.template`
- Custom templates loadable from the project
- Templates render valid imports for the target symbol

Title: Unit and integration scaffolding without fake coverage
User Story: As a developer, I want test skeletons with one explicit TODO per public method, so that gaps are visible and never counted as passing tests.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Scaffolds use `it.todo`/`test.todo` (never empty passing tests)
- Generated files compile; unresolved dependencies are reported
- `smarttest generate --class|--module|--type` targets work

Title: Existing test detection and collision prevention
User Story: As a developer, I want the generator to recognise existing tests and never overwrite them, so that my work is safe.
Acceptance Criteria:
- A source file already covered by a test (any location) is not scaffolded again
- Path collisions are reported; nothing is overwritten by default
- `--force` is not offered for files containing non-generated code

Title: Generator dry-run and atomic writes
User Story: As a developer, I want to preview generated files and have writes be atomic, so that partial generation never corrupts my tree.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `generate --dry-run` lists files and contents without writing
- Writes are all-or-nothing per run
- Generation is repeatable: second run yields no changes

Title: Architecture sync: missing, orphaned and renamed
User Story: As a QA engineer, I want `generate --sync` to report missing tests, orphaned tests and renamed sources, so that test architecture keeps up with refactors.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Reports missing test files, orphaned tests and moved/renamed sources
- Proposes moves/creations; applies nothing without approval
- Works with rename info from Git and snapshots

Title: JSON report with a versioned schema
User Story: As a CI maintainer, I want a machine-readable report of every run, so that I can build tooling on top of SmartTest.
Acceptance Criteria:
- JSON report includes change analysis, decision, executions, coverage scope and timings
- Published JSON Schema with `schemaVersion`
- Skipped-by-selection and executed tests are separate collections

Title: Self-contained HTML report
User Story: As a developer, I want an attractive, offline HTML report, so that I can review and share results easily.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Single file, no network requests; sections: summary, change analysis, selection with reasons, executions, coverage, performance
- Follows the design system (dark/light, reduced motion, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard navigation)
- Untrusted strings (paths, logs, test names) are escaped; no script injection possible
- Generated in < 2 s for the medium benchmark repo

Title: JUnit XML export
User Story: As a CI maintainer, I want JUnit XML output, so that existing CI test dashboards keep working.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Valid JUnit XML for executed tests
- Selection-skipped tests are optional (`--junit-include-skipped`) and marked with a skip reason, never as passed
- Validated against a JUnit XSD in tests

Title: Coverage ingestion with explicit scope
User Story: As a developer, I want coverage from my runner ingested and labelled full or selected, so that partial coverage is never mistaken for project coverage.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Ingests istanbul JSON / lcov from Jest and Vitest
- Every coverage figure is labelled `full` or `selected`; they are never merged
- `smarttest coverage` prints the latest coverage with scope and age

Title: Impact explanations in reports
User Story: As a reviewer, I want selection reasons visible in reports, so that I can audit a run without re-running commands.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Each selected test lists its reasons; skipped tests list skip reasons
- Fallbacks and mandatory triggers are highlighted
- Analysis completeness is shown at the top

Title: Report integrity validation
User Story: As a team lead, I want automated checks that reports never overstate results, so that our quality signals are honest.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Integrity suite asserts: skipped ≠ passed, cached ≠ fresh, partial ≠ full coverage, partial analysis is flagged
- Runs in CI for every report format
- Violations fail the build

Title: Markdown / PR summary export
User Story: As a developer, I want a compact Markdown summary, so that I can paste it into a PR or job summary.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `report --format markdown` produces a summary under 65 kB
- Written to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` when present
- Contains link to the HTML artifact when known

Title: Versioned machine-readable output contracts
User Story: As a CI maintainer, I want stable JSON schemas for `scan`, `impact`, `run` and `explain`, so that scripts don't break between minor versions.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Schemas published in the package and docs
- Breaking schema changes require a major version (checked by a schema-diff test)
- All `--json` outputs validate against their schema in tests

Title: GitHub Actions template
User Story: As a CI maintainer, I want a documented workflow for affected tests on PRs, so that adoption in CI takes minutes.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Template fetches enough history for merge-base, runs `run --affected --mode balanced` on PRs and `--all` on main
- Uses least-privilege permissions and is safe for fork PRs (no secrets required)
- Uploads HTML/JSON/JUnit artifacts and writes the job summary

Title: Basic CI quality gates
User Story: As a tech lead, I want CI to fail on policy findings (missing required categories, forbidden fallbacks), so that policies are enforced, not just reported.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `run --fail-on policy` exits 5 on policy findings
- Gates are configurable per rule
- Gate results appear in all report formats

Title: Regression-detection benchmark harness
User Story: As a QA engineer, I want a harness that injects known regressions into fixtures and checks they're caught, so that we can prove selection safety.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Each fixture defines ≥ 10 seeded mutations with the tests expected to fail
- Harness runs `run --affected` per mutation and records missed failures
- CI fails if any known reproducible failure is missed

Title: Performance benchmarks under documented conditions
User Story: As a product owner, I want reproducible benchmarks for startup, analysis, selection and reports, so that our performance claims are honest.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Benchmark repos (small / medium / large) and reference hardware documented
- Measures warm startup, warm diff analysis, warm selection, report generation, end-to-end savings
- Results published in `benchmarks/RESULTS.md`; targets marked met / not met

Title: Cross-platform validation
User Story: As a Windows developer, I want SmartTest to behave identically on Windows, macOS and Linux, so that I'm not a second-class user.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Path normalisation (separators, case-insensitivity) covered by tests
- Full e2e suite green on the 3-OS CI matrix
- Known platform limitations documented

Title: Performance regression CI
User Story: As a SmartTest contributor, I want CI to flag performance regressions, so that speed doesn't erode release after release.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Benchmarks run nightly; > 15 % regression opens an issue
- Results stored as artifacts for trend comparison
- Noise threshold documented

Title: npm publishing with provenance and changesets
User Story: As a release manager, I want automated, signed releases with changelogs, so that users can verify what they install.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Changesets drive versions and CHANGELOG
- Publishing from CI uses npm provenance / trusted publishing; no long-lived tokens
- Pre-releases published under `next` dist-tag

Title: SBOM, dependency audit and secret scanning
User Story: As a security reviewer, I want an SBOM and automated supply-chain checks, so that enterprises can approve SmartTest.
Acceptance Criteria:
- CycloneDX SBOM attached to each release
- Dependency audit and secret scanning run in CI and block on high severity
- `SECURITY.md` describes disclosure process

Title: Documentation verified against the product
User Story: As a new user, I want docs whose commands actually work, so that I can succeed without asking for help.
Acceptance Criteria:
- Getting-started, CLI reference and configuration reference complete for 1.0
- Doc code blocks tagged `verify` are executed against fixtures in CI
- Time-to-first-affected-run under 5 minutes in a usability test with 3 external developers

Title: Example projects
User Story: As a evaluator, I want runnable example projects in `examples/`, so that I can try SmartTest before touching my repo.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `examples/node`, `react`, `nestjs`, `monorepo`, `no-vcs` each with a README walkthrough
- Examples run in CI against the current build
- Each example demonstrates `run --affected` and `explain`

Title: Clean removal path
User Story: As a developer, I want to remove SmartTest without losing any tests, so that adoption is reversible.
Acceptance Criteria:
- `smarttest uninstall --dry-run` lists config, scripts and `.smarttest/` to remove
- Generated tests are kept by default (they belong to the user)
- Documented manual removal steps
